finding.claim: Unauthenticated OS command injection in GET /ping: the attacker-controlled `host` query parameter is concatenated into a string passed to child_process.exec, which runs it through /bin/sh -c. Arbitrary commands run as the server user and stdout is returned in the response.

trace.note: app.listen(3001) with no host argument: server binds to all interfaces, so the route is network-reachable
app.get('/ping') route with no auth middleware
req.query.host concatenated into command string and passed to exec (shell interpreted)
exec stdout returned to the attacker in res.send(out), giving direct output

finding.guards_checked: No auth middleware (no app.use, route-level only). No allowlist or format validation on host. exec used instead of execFile/argv array. Error branch (tools.js:8-9) does not prevent execution. Other routes /version and /uptime do not take user input, so they are not affected.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only route with user input is /ping (tools.js:6). No auth middleware is registered (no app.use anywhere in tools.js). host is concatenated unvalidated into a string passed to exec, which runs it through /bin/sh (tools.js:7). The err branch (tools.js:8-9) runs only after the command has already executed, so it blocks nothing. A payload such as `127.0.0.1;id` ends in a successful command, so err is null and stdout is sent back (tools.js:11). /version and /uptime take no user input.
verdict.reason: The unauthenticated GET /ping route (tools.js:6) concatenates req.query.host straight into exec (tools.js:7), and the app listens on all interfaces because app.listen(3001) at tools.js:28 has no host argument, so anonymous network attackers can run shell commands and read the output at tools.js:11.
